title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent user (EE1) shares personal identifying information (PII) including email, password, name, government ID, and six-digit code with the Authentication Service (P1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to an untrusted third party.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The Authentication Service (P1) receives the PII and processes or stores it in a way that causes the threat. This includes storing the data in a database, logging it, or potentially reusing it for other services without proper access controls.

title: Account Information Disclosure
description: The parent account owner (P1) shares their account credentials with the authentication service (P1), which then stores them in the MongoDB users collection (DS1). This action causes the threat of unauthorized access to the parent account's sensitive data.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The MongoDB users collection (DS1) receives the parent account's credentials and stores them. This action causes the threat of data being processed and stored in a way that could lead to unauthorized access or misuse.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT tokens and user data with the parent element (ExternalEntity EE1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the parent entity may use this data to identify or link the user to other entities, violating privacy principles.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT tokens and user data with the parent element (ExternalEntity EE1). This act of sharing causes the threat because the parent entity may modify or tamper with the data in transit, violating data integrity principles.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The external entity (EE2) shares its identity (email) with the authentication service (P1) without any authentication or authorization mechanism. This allows P1 to identify and potentially track the user.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The external entity (EE2) shares its password (a sensitive credential) with the authentication service (P1). This exposes the user's authentication credentials to the service.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The authentication service (P1) receives the user's credentials and may use them to access other parts of the system or for unauthorized access to the user's data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares JWT (userType child) data with the Child User (ExternalEntity EE2). This act of sharing causes the threat because the JWT contains sensitive user identity information (userType) that is transmitted to an external entity without appropriate access controls or encryption.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: The destination element (ExternalEntity EE2) receives the JWT and processes it to identify the user. This action causes the threat because the external entity uses the user identifier to link or identify the user, which may be used for profiling or unauthorized access.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: External entity (EE1) shares personal data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) with the profile management process (P3) without explicit consent or a valid legal basis for processing. This act of sharing directly exposes the individual's identity information.

title: Data Processing for Profiling
description: The profile management process (P3) receives the personal data and uses it to create a profile. This processing may involve sensitive attributes (gender, govt ID) that are not necessary for the stated purpose, leading to potential re-identification or profiling of the individual.

title: Child Profile Data Exposure
description: The source element (Process P3) shares the child profile data (id P3) with the data store (DS2) without any explicit consent or authorization from the parent entity. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to unauthorized access.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (MongoDB collection DS2) receives the child profile data and processes it in a way that causes the threat. The system may store, aggregate, or use the data for analytics without proper data minimization or access controls.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: External entity EE2 (Child User) shares personal identity information (e.g., name, ID, email) with the Video Management Service (P2) during the request phase.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: EE2 shares sensitive video metadata (e.g., video ID, thumbnail, duration) with P2, which may be used to identify the user or infer their viewing habits.

title: Data Processing for Inference
description: P2 processes the received video metadata to perform video search, which may correlate with user behavior and allow inference about the user's identity or preferences.

title: Unintended Data Use
description: P2 uses the video metadata for video search, which may be used by the service to track user activity across different video content, potentially violating privacy expectations.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Metadata
description: The source element (Process P2) shares video metadata (e.g., filenames, timestamps, user IDs) with the data flow. If the process does not have sufficient access controls or encryption, an attacker could extract this metadata to identify or link users to specific video content.
assumptions: The process P2 does not enforce strict data segregation between metadata and file storage.

title: Data Exfiltration via Metadata
description: The source element (Process P2) shares video files (or metadata containing file references) with the data flow. If the process is not configured to encrypt data in transit or restrict access to the destination, an attacker could exfiltrate the video files or their metadata.
assumptions: The process P2 does not use secure transmission protocols for the data flow.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Video Files
description: The destination element (DataStore DS3) receives the video files and metadata. If the storage system lacks proper access controls, encryption, or audit logging, an attacker could access the stored video files or metadata.
assumptions: The data store DS3 does not enforce strict access controls or encryption for the video content.

title: Metadata Leakage via Storage
description: The destination element (DataStore DS3) receives the video metadata. If the storage system does not encrypt the metadata or restrict access to it, an attacker could access the metadata to identify users or link them to specific videos.
assumptions: The data store DS3 does not encrypt the metadata associated with the video files.

title: Child Search History Exposure
description: The source element (Process P3) shares its internal state (child search and watch history) with the data store (DS2) without any explicit consent or encryption. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to the destination.
assumptions: The process does not encrypt the search history before sharing.

title: Child Search History Processing
description: The destination element (MongoDB collection DS2) receives the child search history and processes it. This action causes the threat because the data is stored in a way that allows for potential linkage or identification of the child based on the search history.
assumptions: The database does not apply any additional filtering or anonymization to the search history.

title: Unauthorized Access to Video Data
description: External entity EE1 (Parent User) shares video data with Process P2 without explicit authorization or encryption, allowing P2 to potentially access, view, or misuse the content.

title: Data Processing and Storage Risks
description: Process P2 receives video data and may store, process, or transmit it in ways that compromise privacy, such as logging metadata, re-identifying users, or storing data in unencrypted formats.

title: Unauthorized Video Sharing
description: The source element (Process P2) shares video data without explicit, granular consent from the Child User (EE2). This allows the data to be accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF12) transmits video data in a way that allows the source (P2) and destination (EE2) to be linked or identified by metadata (e.g., user ID, video hash) that could be used to track or profile the parties involved.

title: Inappropriate Data Processing
description: The destination element (Child User EE2) receives the video data and processes it in a way that causes privacy risks, such as storing it in a way that enables future profiling or linking to other data sources.

title: Data Collection
description: The source element (DataStore) actively collects browsing data from the child profiles collection, which inherently exposes sensitive user data to the system.
assumptions: The child profiles collection contains unfiltered or partially filtered browsing data.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow itself carries metadata about the parties involved (e.g., user ID, device ID, IP address) that can be used to link or identify the source data with the destination data.
assumptions: The data flow includes metadata fields that are not encrypted or obfuscated.

title: Data Processing
description: The destination element (AI Recommendation Engine) processes the received data, which may involve storing it in a way that allows for future inference or re-identification of the user.
assumptions: The AI engine's processing logic does not include robust de-identification or anonymization steps.

title: Data Collection
description: The process P4 collects browsing data from users without explicit, informed consent from the user.
assumptions: Users are unaware of the specific browsing data being collected.
uncertainty_note: Confident in the assumption that browsing data is collected without consent.

title: Data Processing
description: The process P4 processes the collected browsing data to generate AI recommendations.
assumptions: Processing of user data is necessary for the recommendation engine.
uncertainty_note: Confident in the assumption that processing is necessary.

title: Data Storage
description: The external entity EE3 stores the browsing data in a way that allows for targeted advertising.
assumptions: EE3 stores data in a way that enables personalized advertising.
uncertainty_note: Confident in the assumption that storage enables targeted advertising.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares government ID images with the data store (DS4) without any additional authentication or encryption verification. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to unauthorized access.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (DataStore DS4) receives the government ID images and stores them in a way that causes the threat. The data store may process or store the images without proper access controls, potentially allowing unauthorized users to access or derive sensitive information.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P1) shares the JWT with the Browser localStorage (DataStore DS5). This act of sharing causes the threat because the JWT contains sensitive user credentials (e.g., username, password, or session tokens) that are not intended to be stored in a client-side storage mechanism like localStorage.

title: Data Processing Threat
description: The destination element (DataStore DS5) receives the JWT and stores it in localStorage. This causes a threat because localStorage is a client-side storage mechanism. Storing sensitive authentication credentials in localStorage exposes them to potential XSS attacks, where malicious scripts could read the stored data and impersonate the user.

title: Child Profile Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P3) shares the child profile data with the parent User (ExternalEntity EE1) without verifying the parent's identity or authorization to access the specific child records.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF17) transmits child profile data to the parent User. The parent's identity is not explicitly verified at the source, and the data flow itself may be used to link or identify the parent-user relationship, creating a data-centric threat.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (ExternalEntity EE1) receives the child profile data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing the data in a way that allows future unauthorized access or linking to other user profiles.
